claims.text: The report the lesson opens with — "order 1 shows 900.000 đồng instead of 2.150.000 đồng" — is the one recorded at stage-0 in the comment at the top of samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Debug/WrongTotal.cs.
At stage-0 order 1 in db/seed.sql has two rows in order_items — one unit at 1250000 and two units at 450000 — which add up to 2150000, and the payments row for order 1 is 2150000.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: db/seed.sql lines 37-38 (order_items) and line 52 (payments)

claims.text: At stage-0, samples/DonHang.Samples/Program.cs maps the argument wrong-total to WrongTotal.Run, so `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- wrong-total` run from the repository root runs that sample.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: samples/DonHang.Samples/Program.cs lines 9-25 (dictionary) and lines 27-36 (args[0] lookup)

claims.text: In `dotnet run --project <path> -- <arg>`, everything after the bare `--` is passed to the program being run rather than to the dotnet run command itself.
claims.source_hint: dotnet run documentation, Arguments / the `--` delimiter

claims.text: At stage-0 that sample prints exactly two lines: `expected 2150000, got 1250000` and `one line only: expected 1250000, got 0`.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: run `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- wrong-total`; WrongTotal.cs lines 18-24

claims.text: The printed 1250000 does not match the 900.000 in the recorded report, so the reported figure is not reproducible from the code at stage-0; 900000 is what the order's second line alone would give.
claims.source_hint: compare WrongTotal.cs line 4 with the output of the sample and db/seed.sql line 38 (2 × 450000)

claims.text: In C#, the condition of `for (var i = 0; i < lines.Count - 1; i++)` is evaluated before each iteration, so when lines.Count is 1 the condition `i < 0` is false on the first evaluation and the body never runs.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference, iteration statements: the for statement (condition evaluated before each iteration)

claims.text: In TotalVnd the local totalVnd is initialised to 0, so when the loop body never runs the method returns 0.
`orderOne[..1]` is a range expression producing a slice that contains only the first element of orderOne.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference, operators: index and range operators (the .. range operator, end exclusive)

claims.text: With the two items of order 1, lines.Count - 1 is 1, so i takes only the value 0; the second item is omitted and TotalVnd returns 1250000 instead of 2150000.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: WrongTotal.cs lines 7-16 and line 20; first printed line of the sample

claims.text: For an order of three items (1 × 1250000, 2 × 450000, 1 × 320000) the same loop adds the first two and omits the third, returning 2150000 where the correct total is 2470000.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: WrongTotal.cs lines 10-12, evaluated with lines.Count = 3; arithmetic 1250000 + 900000 + 320000

claims.text: Opinion: when a failure cannot be produced on demand, a code change cannot be judged a fix, because the run after the change may have passed for reasons unrelated to the change.

Opinion: each halving is information — if the failure survives, the half you kept is enough to trigger it, so keep halving there; if it disappears, the part you removed matters, so put half of it back and run again.

Opinion: a hypothesis stated so that one check could show it false, with its result predicted before the check runs, removes one possible cause whether it survives or not; changing code before that point cannot be distinguished from guessing.
Opinion: the record of what you ran, expected and got is what a later question or written report is made of, so keeping it during the session costs less than reconstructing it afterwards.

Opinion: of the two printed lines the 0 is the easier to explain, because for this input — a single line of 1 × 1250000 — the only way the sum stays 0 is a loop body that never ran, while 1250000 is a plausible number that still needs explaining.
claims.source_hint: no official source; criterion stated in the same sentence of the lesson

claims.text: Opinion: a bug in code you are re-reading often lives in the gap between what the code says and what you assumed it said, so re-reading with the same assumption does not find it. Not all bugs are of this kind.
claims.source_hint: misconception 1 of the outline entry for foundation.l2.debugging-method

claims.text: `dotnet run --project <PATH>` takes the path of the project to run, given either as a folder name or as the full path to the project file.
